inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: The US is pushing a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran through Pakistan, but Iran has responded with five counter-conditions demanding an end to aggression, compensation for past harms, and recognition of their sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. Israel refuses to engage at all and is instead doubling down on pre-emptive strikes, which makes clear how these entrenched powers keep choosing military dominance and old patterns of control instead of any real move toward equity. This approach just deepens the structural inequalities that hurt vulnerable populations across the region and blocks the institutional reforms needed to fix root causes like unequal power dynamics and the history of outside interventions that fuel instability rather than protect the rights of those most affected. We need to stay skeptical of any talk about "strength" that ignores these realities and locks us into endless escalation.
